To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have demonstrated the feasibility of a high-precision astrometric survey of a large number of fields in the Kapteyan Selected Areas, that we have demonstrated that these data can be used to study the kinematics of the Monoceros ring, and that we have detected a significant overdensity of proper-motion selected stars in the trailing tail of Sagittarius.

(1) our survey provides a unique, high-precision, absolute astrometric data set that will enable detailed dynamical modeling, and (2) our preliminary results show that the Sagittarius trailing tail and the Monoceros stream are real structures in phase space.
the Sagittarius trailing tail is ~20-25 kpc long and that the Monoceros ring appears to have a complex structure with a possible bifurcation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of the Milky Way and its satellites.
the dynamics of satellite galaxies and streams in the outer halo of the Milky Way.
the detailed dynamical history of the Sagittarus dwarf spheroidal galaxy, the Monoceros ring, and other stellar streams in the Milky Way.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Sagittarius tidal tail is a very complex system, and the Monoceros ring is not a ring at all, but is composed of two distinct components: one is a tidal tail of the Sagitarius dwarf, and the other is a very extended, thin, and elongated structure of stars that are in the halo and/or the disk of our Galaxy.

the Sagittarius tidal stream is a very complex system, with at least two distinct streams, one of them being the Monoceros stream, which has been previously identified as a tidal stream from the Sagittarius galaxy.
the survey is working well, and that we have already found some interesting things.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the absolute proper motions in our survey fields are typically accurate to ~2 mas yr^(--1) for stars with V~19-21.
we are in the midst of an exciting era in Galactic archaeology, with the ability to use our Galaxy's satellites to probe the structure, dynamics, and history of its dark matter halo.
the absolute proper motions of stars in these two structures have been determined to precisions of ~0.5-0.8 mas yr^(- 1) to V ~ 19 mag.
The main takeaway from our work is that
these data are sufficiently accurate to detect the tidal stream of Sagittarius in the northern hemisphere and to measure its velocity dispersion and proper motions.
the tidal tail is not a continuous stream, but is rather composed of a series of discrete substructures, some of which are likely to be dynamically independent.
the Sagittarius tidal stream in the northern sky is much more complicated than previously thought.
